record.context_brief: eventual periodicity of Sq^0 on Ext over the Steenrod algebra
record.original_question: Fix a homological degree s and let Sq^0: Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) -> Ext_A^{s,2t}(F_2, F_2) be the squaring operation induced by the Frobenius map on the dual Steenrod algebra. If Im((Sq^0)^i) denotes the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2), does there exist a number r = r(s) such that for every i >= r the map (Sq^0)^{i-r}: Im((Sq^0)^r) -> Im((Sq^0)^i) is an isomorphism? Equivalently, for fixed s, is every finite Sq^0-family in Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) bounded in length by some r(s)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 (Sq0 is eventually isomorphic on the Ext groups.) Let Im(Sq0)i denote the image of (Sq0)i on ExtsA(F2, F2). Then, for arbitrary s, there exists a number r = r(s) depending on s such that (Sq0)i-r : Im(Sq0)r -> Im(Sq0)i is an isomorphism for every i >= r.
In other words, the conjecture predicts that any finite Sq0-family in ExtsA(F2, F2) has at most r(s) nonzero elements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ denote the mod $2$ Steenrod algebra and let $\mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,t}(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$ be the bigraded $\mathbb{F}_2$-vector space of $\mathrm{Ext}$ groups of the trivial $A$-module $\mathbb{F}_2$. Write $\mathrm{Ext}_A^s(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2) = \bigoplus_t \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,t}(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$. Let 
$$\mathrm{Sq}^0 : \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,t}(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,2t}(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$$
denote the Frobenius-induced squaring operation on $\mathrm{Ext}$, induced by the Frobenius (squaring) endomorphism of the dual Steenrod algebra. For each integer $i \geq 0$, let $\mathrm{Im}((\mathrm{Sq}^0)^i) \subseteq \mathrm{Ext}_A^s(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$ be the image of the $i$-fold iterate of $\mathrm{Sq}^0$.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed homological degree $s \geq 0$, there exists an integer $r = r(s)$ such that for all $i \geq r$ the iterated map
$$(\mathrm{Sq}^0)^{i-r} : \mathrm{Im}((\mathrm{Sq}^0)^r) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Im}((\mathrm{Sq}^0)^i)$$
is an isomorphism. Equivalently (defining a "finite $\mathrm{Sq}^0$-family" in $\mathrm{Ext}_A^s(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$ to be a maximal sequence of nonzero elements $x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_n$ with $\mathrm{Sq}^0(x_j) = x_{j+1}$ and $(\mathrm{Sq}^0)^{n+1}$ vanishing on $x_0$), show that for fixed $s$ the lengths of all finite $\mathrm{Sq}^0$-families in $\mathrm{Ext}_A^s(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$ are uniformly bounded by some $r(s)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a strengthening of Minami's "new doomsday conjecture" concerning the action of $\mathrm{Sq}^0$ on $\mathrm{Ext}$ over the Steenrod algebra. Minami's related conjecture about permanent cycles in the image of $(\mathrm{Sq}^0)^n$ is widely cited as still open in the algebraic topology literature, and no proof or disproof of the eventual-isomorphism statement appears in the searched sources. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Doomsday conjecture - HandWiki
status_evidence.snippet: Minami (1995) stated a modified version called the new doomsday conjecture... that there are no nontrivial permanent cycles in the image of (Sq^0)^n for n sufficiently large depending on s.
status_evidence.claim: The related Minami new doomsday conjecture concerning iterates of Sq^0 on Ext over the Steenrod algebra is recorded as an open problem.
